# SPEECH — the two audio verticals

> **Current work.** `PIPELINE.md` (the z-image slice) is **parked** at 14.26 s
> an image; this is what happens next. Same rules as that file: it is
> rewritten rather than appended to, history goes to `TODO.md` and closed
> findings to `research/`.

**Targets**: `wav → text` for `parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3` and `text → wav` for
`Kokoro-82M`, both end to end in Go on Vulkan, both validated against a Python
reference dump before anything is optimised. Two of `GOALS.md`'s five models,
and the two smallest.

**Status (2026-09-20, T10)**: **both verticals are on the device, the loop
between them closes over HTTP, and synthesis now costs the same per second of
audio however long the utterance is.**
T9 staged kokoro once for the life of the server instead of once per request:
`POST /v1/audio/speech` went from **550 ms to 59** for 6.45 s of audio, byte
for byte the same waveform.
Speech-to-text transcribes an 11 s clip in 43 ms, 257x real time, whole model
resident, S1–S8 done. **Text-to-speech is 31 ms for 3.25 s of audio**, 105x
real time. T6 is finished: ALBERT 104 ms to 4 (T6a), the F0/N AdaIN stacks 40
to 1 (T6b), the six bidirectional LSTMs 73 to 6 (T6c) and the chain between
them 17 to 8 (T6d) — so **the phoneme side went from 222 ms to 8 and is now
26% of an utterance, over 1.96 ms of GPU time**. The other 74% is the vocoder,
whose 22 ms T4c and T7 cut from 3626.
T8 closed the last open feature: a voice may name a **mixture** of packs, in
upstream's own spelling, and T9 closed the last place where the server cost
more than the model.

**R1 closed the loop and moved the target.** `cmd/roundtrip` runs text through
both endpoints and back — six prose cases return exactly — and what it
measured is that the two verticals scaled in opposite directions:
transcription amortises its fixed cost away to 257x, while synthesis bottomed
out at 8.3 ms per second of audio and then got **36% worse per second** by a
nineteen-second utterance. `cmd/tts` localised that to **PL-BERT, 4 ms at 50
tokens and 75 at 321**. See [R1](#r1--the-round-trip-and-what-it-says-to-do-next).

**T10 removed it.** PL-BERT's attention was a scalar kernel chosen when the
sequence was fifty tokens; on the matrix cores it is **216x faster at 321
tokens and 420x at 510**, which takes the whole encoder from 66.8 ms to
**2.5** and an ALBERT layer from 16.2 ms to **288 us** at the model's ceiling.
A nineteen-second utterance is **225 ms → 162** (86.9x → **120.5x** real
time), the round trip is **61.6x → 70.1x**, and the speech leg is a straight
line instead of a curve: 8.0 ms per second of audio from five seconds to
nineteen, where it used to climb to 11.3. Not one duration moved.
See [T10](#t10--pl-berts-attention-on-the-matrix-cores-done).

`go run ./cmd/tts -gpu -text 'Hello there.'` speaks, with no Python on the
path. T5 opened with a measurement instead of code — **91% of running-text
tokens are a dictionary lookup and a part-of-speech tagger decides 1.74% of
them** — and ended with the whole of misaki's English G2P ported: five
components exact against their own dumped oracles, twelve measured rules where
spacy's tagger mattered, and a cgo binding to libespeak-ng for the rest.
**The designed corpus is exact, 24 of 24; on 400 sentences nobody chose, 92.4%
of phoneme words agree.** [Write-up](research/t5-kokoro-g2p.md).

	"strix-halo-vulkan/vk"
)

const strixHaloDeviceID = 0x1586

const (
	elementCount = 256
	localSizeX   = 64 // must match shaders/double.comp's local_size_x
)

func main() {
	if err := run(); err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}

	if err != nil {
		return err
	}

	fmt.Printf("using device: %s (vendor 0x%04x, device 0x%04x)\n", phys.Name, phys.VendorID, phys.DeviceID)

	queueFamily, err := phys.ComputeQueueFamily()
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}

	device, err := vk.NewDevice(phys, queueFamily, vk.DeviceFeatures{})
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	defer device.Destroy()

	buf, err := device.NewBuffer(elementCount * 4)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	defer buf.Destroy()

	input := make([]float32, elementCount)
	for i := range input {

	}

	shader, err := device.NewShaderModule(shaders.Double)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}

	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	defer pipe.Destroy()

	groups := uint32((elementCount + localSizeX - 1) / localSizeX)
	if err := pipe.Dispatch(groups); err != nil {

	}

	for i, v := range out {

		if v != want {

		}
	}
	fmt.Printf("verified: %d elements doubled correctly (e.g. %v -> %v)\n", elementCount, input[1], out[1])

	for i := range devices {

	}

class AsyncEventHandler(ABC):

        self, reader: asyncio.StreamReader, writer: asyncio.StreamWriter
    ) -> None:
        self.reader = reader
        self.writer = writer

    async def handle_event(self, event: Event) -> bool:
        """Handle an event. Returning false will disconnect the client."""
        return True

        await async_write_event(event, self.writer)

        self._is_running = True

                if event is None:

            self.writer.close()

        """Called when client disconnects."""

from collections import defaultdict
from collections.abc import AsyncGenerator
import io
import logging
from typing import override
import wave

from wyoming.audio import AudioChunk, AudioStart, AudioStop
from wyoming.client import AsyncTcpClient
from wyoming.error import Error
from wyoming.info import TtsProgram
from wyoming.tts import (
    Synthesize,
    SynthesizeChunk,
    SynthesizeStart,
    SynthesizeStop,
    SynthesizeStopped,
    SynthesizeVoice,
)

from homeassistant.components import tts
from homeassistant.core import HomeAssistant, callback
from homeassistant.exceptions import HomeAssistantError
from homeassistant.helpers.entity_platform import AddConfigEntryEntitiesCallback

from .const import ATTR_SPEAKER
from .coordinator import WyomingInfoCoordinator
from .data import WyomingService
from .error import WyomingError, error_event_message
from .models import WyomingConfigEntry

_LOGGER = logging.getLogger(__name__)


async def async_setup_entry(
    hass: HomeAssistant,
    config_entry: WyomingConfigEntry,
    async_add_entities: AddConfigEntryEntitiesCallback,
) -> None:
    """Set up Wyoming speech-to-text."""
    item = config_entry.runtime_data
    async_add_entities(
        [
            WyomingTtsProvider(config_entry, item.coordinator, item.service),
        ]
    )


class WyomingTtsProvider(tts.TextToSpeechEntity):
    """Wyoming text-to-speech provider."""

    _attr_default_options = {}
    _attr_supported_options = [tts.ATTR_AUDIO_OUTPUT, tts.ATTR_VOICE, ATTR_SPEAKER]

    def __init__(
        self,
        config_entry: WyomingConfigEntry,
        coordinator: WyomingInfoCoordinator,
        service: WyomingService,
    ) -> None:
        """Set up provider."""
        self.config_entry = config_entry
        self.coordinator = coordinator
        self.service = service

        # The platform is only set up when an installed TTS service exists.
        self._tts_service = next(tts for tts in service.info.tts if tts.installed)
        self._voices: dict[str, list[tts.Voice]] = {}
        self._rebuild_voices(self._tts_service)

        self._attr_name = self._tts_service.name
        self._attr_unique_id = f"{config_entry.entry_id}-tts"  # pylint: disable=home-assistant-entity-unique-id-redundant-platform

    @override
    async def async_added_to_hass(self) -> None:
        """Subscribe to info updates."""
        await super().async_added_to_hass()
        self.async_on_remove(
            self.coordinator.async_add_listener(self._handle_info_update)
        )

    @callback
    def _handle_info_update(self) -> None:
        """Rebuild the voice list when the service reports new info."""
        tts_service = next(
            (tts for tts in self.coordinator.data.tts if tts.installed), None
        )
        if tts_service is None:
            # Keep the last known voices if the service reports none.
            return

        self._tts_service = tts_service
        self._rebuild_voices(tts_service)

    @callback
    def _rebuild_voices(self, tts_service: TtsProgram) -> None:
        """Collect the installed voices, grouped by language."""
        voice_languages: set[str] = set()
        voices: dict[str, list[tts.Voice]] = defaultdict(list)
        for voice in tts_service.voices:
            if not voice.installed:
                continue

            voice_languages.update(voice.languages)
            for language in voice.languages:
                voices[language].append(
                    tts.Voice(
                        voice_id=voice.name,
                        name=voice.description or voice.name,
                    )
                )

        # Sort voices by name
        for language_voices in voices.values():
            language_voices.sort(key=lambda v: v.name)

        self._voices = voices
        self._attr_supported_languages = sorted(voice_languages)

        # Only move the default when the current one is gone so that installing
        # an unrelated voice cannot change it.
        current_default = getattr(self, "_attr_default_language", None)
        if voice_languages and current_default not in voice_languages:
            self._attr_default_language = self._attr_supported_languages[0]

    @callback
    @override
    def async_get_supported_voices(self, language: str) -> list[tts.Voice] | None:
        """Return a list of supported voices for a language."""
        return self._voices.get(language)

    @override
    async def async_get_tts_audio(self, message, language, options):
        """Load TTS from TCP socket."""
        voice_name: str | None = options.get(tts.ATTR_VOICE)
        voice_speaker: str | None = options.get(ATTR_SPEAKER)

        try:
            async with AsyncTcpClient(self.service.host, self.service.port) as client:
                voice: SynthesizeVoice | None = None
                if voice_name is not None:
                    voice = SynthesizeVoice(name=voice_name, speaker=voice_speaker)

                synthesize = Synthesize(text=message, voice=voice)
                await client.write_event(synthesize.event())

                with io.BytesIO() as wav_io:
                    wav_writer: wave.Wave_write | None = None
                    while True:
                        event = await client.read_event()
                        if event is None:
                            _LOGGER.debug("Connection lost")
                            return (None, None)

                        if Error.is_type(event.type):
                            raise HomeAssistantError(
                                error_event_message(Error.from_event(event))
                            )

                        if AudioStop.is_type(event.type):
                            break

                        if AudioChunk.is_type(event.type):
                            chunk = AudioChunk.from_event(event)
                            if wav_writer is None:
                                wav_writer = wave.open(wav_io, "wb")
                                wav_writer.setframerate(chunk.rate)
                                wav_writer.setsampwidth(chunk.width)
                                wav_writer.setnchannels(chunk.channels)

                            wav_writer.writeframes(chunk.audio)

                    if wav_writer is not None:
                        wav_writer.close()

                    data = wav_io.getvalue()

        except OSError, WyomingError:
            return (None, None)

        return ("wav", data)

    @override
    def async_supports_streaming_input(self) -> bool:
        """Return if the TTS engine supports streaming input."""
        return self._tts_service.supports_synthesize_streaming

    @override
    async def async_stream_tts_audio(
        self, request: tts.TTSAudioRequest
    ) -> tts.TTSAudioResponse:
        """Generate speech from an incoming message."""
        voice_name: str | None = request.options.get(tts.ATTR_VOICE)
        voice_speaker: str | None = request.options.get(ATTR_SPEAKER)
        voice: SynthesizeVoice | None = None
        if voice_name is not None:
            voice = SynthesizeVoice(name=voice_name, speaker=voice_speaker)

        client = AsyncTcpClient(self.service.host, self.service.port)
        await client.connect()

        # Stream text chunks to client
        self.config_entry.async_create_background_task(
            self.hass,
            self._write_tts_message(request.message_gen, client, voice),
            "wyoming tts write",
        )

        async def data_gen():
            # Stream audio bytes from client
            try:
                async for data_chunk in self._read_tts_audio(client):
                    yield data_chunk
            finally:
                await client.disconnect()

        return tts.TTSAudioResponse("wav", data_gen())

    async def _write_tts_message(
        self,
        message_gen: AsyncGenerator[str],
        client: AsyncTcpClient,
        voice: SynthesizeVoice | None,
    ) -> None:
        """Write text chunks to the client."""
        try:
            # Start stream
            await client.write_event(SynthesizeStart(voice=voice).event())

            # Accumulate entire message for synthesize event.
            message = ""
            async for message_chunk in message_gen:
                message += message_chunk

                await client.write_event(SynthesizeChunk(text=message_chunk).event())

            # Send entire message for backwards compatibility
            await client.write_event(Synthesize(text=message, voice=voice).event())

            # End stream
            await client.write_event(SynthesizeStop().event())
        except OSError, WyomingError:
            # Disconnected
            _LOGGER.warning("Unexpected disconnection from TTS client")

    async def _read_tts_audio(self, client: AsyncTcpClient) -> AsyncGenerator[bytes]:
        """Read audio events from the client and yield WAV audio chunks.

        The WAV header is sent first with a frame count of 0 to indicate that
        we're streaming and don't know the number of frames ahead of time.
        """
        wav_header_sent = False

        try:
            while event := await client.read_event():
                if Error.is_type(event.type):
                    raise HomeAssistantError(
                        error_event_message(Error.from_event(event))
                    )

                if wav_header_sent and AudioChunk.is_type(event.type):
                    # PCM audio
                    yield AudioChunk.from_event(event).audio
                elif (not wav_header_sent) and AudioStart.is_type(event.type):
                    # WAV header with nframes = 0 for streaming
                    audio_start = AudioStart.from_event(event)
                    with io.BytesIO() as wav_io:
                        wav_file: wave.Wave_write = wave.open(wav_io, "wb")
                        with wav_file:
                            wav_file.setframerate(audio_start.rate)
                            wav_file.setsampwidth(audio_start.width)
                            wav_file.setnchannels(audio_start.channels)

                        wav_io.seek(0)
                        yield wav_io.getvalue()

                    wav_header_sent = True
                elif SynthesizeStopped.is_type(event.type):
                    # All TTS audio has been received
                    break
        except OSError, WyomingError:
            # Disconnected
            _LOGGER.warning("Unexpected disconnection from TTS client")

                                wav_writer.setsampwidth(chunk.width)
                                wav_writer.setnchannels(chunk.channels)

                            wav_writer.writeframes(chunk.audio)

                    if wav_writer is not None:
                        wav_writer.close()

                    data = wav_io.getvalue()

            return (None, None)

    def async_supports_streaming_input(self) -> bool:

        self, request: tts.TTSAudioRequest
    ) -> tts.TTSAudioResponse:

            self.hass,
            self._write_tts_message(request.message_gen, client, voice),

        message_gen: AsyncGenerator[str],
        client: AsyncTcpClient,
        voice: SynthesizeVoice | None,
    ) -> None:

        try:

            await client.write_event(SynthesizeStart(voice=voice).event())

            message = ""
            async for message_chunk in message_gen:

            await client.write_event(SynthesizeStop().event())
        except OSError, WyomingError:

        wav_header_sent = False

            while event := await client.read_event():

                        error_event_message(Error.from_event(event))
                    )

                if wav_header_sent and AudioChunk.is_type(event.type):

                    yield AudioChunk.from_event(event).audio
                elif (not wav_header_sent) and AudioStart.is_type(event.type):
                    # WAV header with nframes = 0 for streaming
                    audio_start = AudioStart.from_event(event)
                    with io.BytesIO() as wav_io:
                        wav_file: wave.Wave_write = wave.open(wav_io, "wb")
                        with wav_file:
                            wav_file.setframerate(audio_start.rate)
                            wav_file.setsampwidth(audio_start.width)
                            wav_file.setnchannels(audio_start.channels)

                        wav_io.seek(0)
                        yield wav_io.getvalue()

                    wav_header_sent = True
                elif SynthesizeStopped.is_type(event.type):
                    # All TTS audio has been received
                    break
        except OSError, WyomingError:
            # Disconnected
            _LOGGER.warning("Unexpected disconnection from TTS client")

68		DefaultPort = 10300

3	// The event types this server reads and writes. Wyoming has more of them --
4	// wake word detection, intent handling, satellite control -- and the rule for
5	// a type that is not here is to drop it silently rather than to refuse it,
6	// which is what the protocol asks of a server and what lets a newer client
7	// talk to an older one.
8	const (
9		typeDescribe      = "describe"
10		typeInfo          = "info"
11		typePing          = "ping"
12		typePong          = "pong"
13		typeError         = "error"
14		typeSelectProgram = "select-program"
15	
16		typeTranscribe = "transcribe"
17		typeTranscript = "transcript"
18	
19		typeSynthesize = "synthesize"
20	
21		typeAudioStart = "audio-start"
22		typeAudioChunk = "audio-chunk"
23		typeAudioStop  = "audio-stop"
24	)
25	
26	// Attribution is who made an artifact and where it came from. Every artifact
27	// in an `info` message carries one, and the reference client's decoder
28	// requires it -- an artifact without it fails to construct, rather than
29	// arriving with an empty one.
30	type Attribution struct {
31		Name string `json:"name"`
32		URL  string `json:"url"`
33	}
34	
35	// Artifact is what a program and a model have in common.
36	//
37	// Description and Version are pointers so that "we do not have one" is sent
38	// as an explicit null rather than by leaving the field out. The reference
39	// decoder treats those two the same way, but a null says the server
40	// considered the question and a missing key does not.
41	type Artifact struct {
42		Name        string      `json:"name"`
43		Description *string     `json:"description"`
44		Attribution Attribution `json:"attribution"`
45		Installed   bool        `json:"installed"`
46		Version     *string     `json:"version"`
47	}
48	
49	// AsrModel is one speech-to-text model and the languages it hears.
50	type AsrModel struct {
51		Artifact
52		Languages []string `json:"languages"`
53	}
54	
55	// AsrProgram is a speech-to-text service.
56	//
57	// The three `prefers`/`requires` flags are advice to a satellite about the
58	// audio it sends, and they are answered from what this checkpoint actually
59	// is. **RequiresExternalVAD is true**: parakeet transcribes a clip that has
60	// already been cut, and nothing in this repository decides where a voice
61	// command ended, so the satellite or Home Assistant has to. The other two are
62	// true for the ordinary reason -- a far-field microphone's gain and noise are
63	// a room's problem and not a model's.
64	type AsrProgram struct {
65		Artifact
66		Models                       []AsrModel `json:"models"`
67		SupportsTranscriptStreaming  bool       `json:"supports_transcript_streaming"`
68		RequiresExternalVAD          bool       `json:"requires_external_vad"`
69		PrefersAutoGainEnabled       bool       `json:"prefers_auto_gain_enabled"`
70		PrefersNoiseReductionEnabled bool       `json:"prefers_noise_reduction_enabled"`
71	}
72	
73	// TtsVoiceSpeaker is one speaker inside a multi-speaker voice. Kokoro has
74	// none: a voice pack is one speaker, and a blend of packs is spelled in the
75	// voice name rather than selected here, so this type exists to be absent.
76	type TtsVoiceSpeaker struct {
77		Name string `json:"name"`
78	}
79	
80	// TtsVoice is one voice pack. Home Assistant shows Description in its voice
81	// menu and sends Name back as the voice id, so the two are a readable label
82	// and the checkpoint's own filename respectively.
83	type TtsVoice struct {
84		Artifact
85		Languages []string          `json:"languages"`
86		Speakers  []TtsVoiceSpeaker `json:"speakers"`
87	}
88	
89	// TtsProgram is a text-to-speech service.
90	//
91	// **SupportsSynthesizeStreaming is false**, and that is a measurement rather
92	// than a gap. Streaming synthesis in this protocol means the client sends the
93	// text in pieces as it is generated and the server answers each piece with
94	// audio; what it buys is the time between the first piece and the last. On
95	// this part kokoro synthesises nineteen seconds of speech in 162 ms
96	// (SPEECH.md T10), so the whole utterance is ready before a satellite could
97	// have finished playing the first sentence of a streamed one, and the
98	// streaming path would only add a way for the pieces to disagree about
99	// prosody -- the durations are decided for the whole utterance at once.
100	type TtsProgram struct {
101		Artifact
102		Voices                      []TtsVoice `json:"voices"`
103		SupportsSynthesizeStreaming bool       `json:"supports_synthesize_streaming"`
104	}
105	
106	// Info is the answer to `describe`: what this process loaded.
107	//
108	// The five empty lists are not padding. The reference decoder iterates each
109	// of them, so a missing key is fine (it defaults to empty) but a null is a
110	// crash on the client, and the honest way to say "this server has no wake
111	// word detector" is an empty list rather than silence.
112	type Info struct {
113		ASR    []AsrProgram `json:"asr"`
114		TTS    []TtsProgram `json:"tts"`
115		Handle []any        `json:"handle"`
116		Intent []any        `json:"intent"`
117		Wake   []any        `json:"wake"`
118		Mic    []any        `json:"mic"`
119		Snd    []any        `json:"snd"`
120	}

124	// than the alternative and makes the field names checkable.
125	
126	// pingData is `ping` and `pong`: the text, if any, is copied back verbatim.
127	type pingData struct {
128		Text *string `json:"text"`
129	}

132	// one of these, because the alternative -- closing the connection -- is
133	// reported by Home Assistant as "connection lost" and says nothing about what
134	// went wrong.
135	type errorData struct {

138	}

144	}

2	// which is what Home Assistant's voice pipeline speaks.
3	//
4	// It is a second door onto the same backends `api` serves over HTTP, and it
5	// exists because Home Assistant does not speak OpenAI's audio API: its
6	// `wyoming` integration connects to a TCP port, asks what is behind it, and
7	// then streams microphone audio in and synthesised speech out. Nothing in
8	// here owns a model or touches Vulkan -- a Server holds the same
9	// api.SpeechBackend and api.TranscriptionBackend the HTTP handlers do, so the
10	// two protocols are one process, one staging of the weights and one GPU
11	// queue.
12	//
13	// The wire format is a newline-terminated JSON header, then an optional JSON
14	// data block, then an optional binary payload:
15	//
16	//	{"type":"audio-chunk","version":"1.10.2","data_length":57,"payload_length":2048}\n
17	//	{"rate": 16000, "width": 2, "channels": 1, "timestamp": 0}
18	//	<2048 bytes of little-endian signed 16-bit PCM>
19	//
20	// The lengths are what makes it framed rather than line-oriented: the payload
21	// is raw PCM and may contain a newline. `data` may also appear inline in the
22	// header, in which case the trailing block is merged over it, which is what
23	// the reference implementation does and what ReadEvent reproduces.

26	// like, voices.go is how a kokoro voice pack is described to a client, and
27	// server.go is the conversation.

36	)

38	// protocolVersion is the `version` every event this server writes carries.

41	// implements, rather than a version of this server: the field is there so a
42	// client can tell what the framing is, and answering with our own release
43	// number would tell it nothing it could act on. No client this has been run
44	// against reads it.

47	// The three bounds an event is read under. They exist because this is a
48	// protocol whose frames declare their own length: a header that says
49	// "payload_length: 4294967296" is one allocation away from the process, and

71		Payload []byte
72	}

89	// A nil data value writes a header and nothing else.

129		}
130		if h.Type == "" {

135		if n := h.DataLength; n != nil && *n > 0 {

137				return nil, fmt.Errorf("wyoming: %s declares %d bytes of data, over the %d-byte limit",
138					h.Type, *n, maxDataBytes)
139			}
140			buf := make([]byte, *n)
141			if _, err := io.ReadFull(r, buf); err != nil {
142				return nil, fmt.Errorf("wyoming: %s: reading %d bytes of data: %w", h.Type, *n, err)
143			}
144			if ev.Data, err = mergeData(h.Data, buf); err != nil {
145				return nil, fmt.Errorf("wyoming: %s: %w", h.Type, err)
146			}
147		}
148	
149		if n := h.PayloadLength; n != nil && *n > 0 {
150			if *n > maxPayloadBytes {
151				return nil, fmt.Errorf("wyoming: %s declares %d bytes of payload, over the %d-byte limit",
152					h.Type, *n, maxPayloadBytes)
153			}
154			ev.Payload = make([]byte, *n)
155			if _, err := io.ReadFull(r, ev.Payload); err != nil {
156				return nil, fmt.Errorf("wyoming: %s: reading %d bytes of payload: %w", h.Type, *n, err)
157			}
158		}
159		return ev, nil
160	}

163	//
164	// The flush is not optional: every event this server sends is either an
165	// answer somebody is blocked on or a chunk of audio somebody is playing, so

167	func WriteEvent(w *bufio.Writer, ev *Event) error {
168		h := header{Type: ev.Type, Version: protocolVersion}
169		data := ev.Data
170		if isEmptyObject(data) {
171			data = nil
172		}

175			h.DataLength = &n
176		}
177		if len(ev.Payload) > 0 {
178			n := len(ev.Payload)

183			return fmt.Errorf("wyoming: encoding the %s header: %w", ev.Type, err)
184		}
185		if _, err := w.Write(line); err != nil {

187		}
188		if err := w.WriteByte('\n'); err != nil {
189			return err
190		}
191		if _, err := w.Write(data); err != nil {
192			return err
193		}
194		if _, err := w.Write(ev.Payload); err != nil {

196		}

            assert ev is not None, "connection closed"
            if Info.is_type(ev.type):
                info = Info.from_event(ev)

    print("== describe ==")
    print(f"  asr programs: {len(info.asr)}  tts programs: {len(info.tts)}")
    for p in info.asr:
        print(f"  asr {p.name!r} installed={p.installed} vad={p.requires_external_vad} "

        for m in p.models:

    for p in info.tts:
        print(f"  tts {p.name!r} installed={p.installed} stream={p.supports_synthesize_streaming} "
              f"voices={len(p.voices)}")
        for v in p.voices[:3]:
            print(f"    voice {v.name!r} {v.description!r} {v.languages} speakers={v.speakers}")
        langs = sorted({l for v in p.voices for l in v.languages})
        print(f"    languages: {langs}")

    assert any(a.installed for a in info.asr), "no installed asr"
    assert any(t.installed for t in info.tts), "no installed tts"
    return info


async def ping():
    async with AsyncTcpClient(HOST, PORT) as c:
        await c.write_event(Ping(text="hello").event())
        ev = await c.read_event()
        assert Pong.is_type(ev.type), ev.type
        assert Pong.from_event(ev).text == "hello"
    print("== ping ==\n  pong, text copied")


async def synthesize(text, voice_name=None):
    """HA's WyomingTtsProvider.async_get_tts_audio, verbatim in shape."""
    async with AsyncTcpClient(HOST, PORT) as c:
        voice = SynthesizeVoice(name=voice_name) if voice_name else None
        await c.write_event(Synthesize(text=text, voice=voice).event())

            wav_writer = None
            chunks = 0
            while True:

                assert ev is not None, "connection lost"

                    chunks += 1

                        wav_writer.setframerate(chunk.rate)
                        wav_writer.setsampwidth(chunk.width)
                        wav_writer.setnchannels(chunk.channels)

            ev = await c.read_event()
            assert ev is not None, "connection lost"

"""The two doors must produce the same waveform, and the Wyoming door must
accept a rate the model does not read."""
import asyncio, io, json, urllib.request, wave
import sys
sys.path.insert(0, "")
from drive import synthesize, transcribe, HOST, PORT
from wyoming.client import AsyncTcpClient
from wyoming.asr import Transcribe, Transcript
from wyoming.audio import AudioStart, AudioChunk, AudioStop
from wyoming.error import Error

TEXT = "The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog."
VOICE = "af_heart"


def http_speech(text, voice):
    body = json.dumps({"input": text, "voice": voice, "response_format": "wav"}).encode()
    req = urllib.request.Request("http://127.0.0.1:18080/v1/audio/speech", data=body,
                                 headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"})
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req) as r:
        return r.read()


def frames(wav_bytes):
    with wave.open(io.BytesIO(wav_bytes)) as w:
        return w.getframerate(), w.getnframes(), w.readframes(w.getnframes())


async def transcribe_at(wav_bytes, rate):
    """Send the clip at whatever rate it is; the server resamples."""
    with wave.open(io.BytesIO(wav_bytes)) as w:
        assert w.getframerate() == rate, (w.getframerate(), rate)
        pcm = w.readframes(w.getnframes())
    async with AsyncTcpClient(HOST, PORT) as c:
        await c.write_event(Transcribe(language="en").event())
        await c.write_event(AudioStart(rate=rate, width=2, channels=1).event())
        for off in range(0, len(pcm), 2048):
            await c.write_event(AudioChunk(rate=rate, width=2, channels=1,
                                           audio=pcm[off:off + 2048]).event())
        await c.write_event(AudioStop().event())
        while True:
            ev = await c.read_event()
            assert ev is not None, "connection lost"
            if Error.is_type(ev.type):
                raise RuntimeError(Error.from_event(ev).text)
            if Transcript.is_type(ev.type):
                return Transcript.from_event(ev).text


async def main():
    wy = await synthesize(TEXT, VOICE)
    http = http_speech(TEXT, VOICE)
    a, b = frames(wy), frames(http)
    print("== the two doors ==")
    print(f"  wyoming: {a[0]} Hz, {a[1]} frames   http: {b[0]} Hz, {b[1]} frames")
    assert a[0] == b[0] and a[1] == b[1], (a[:2], b[:2])
    assert a[2] == b[2], "the samples differ"
    print("  byte for byte the same waveform")

    print("== the loop, over wyoming, at the vocoder's own 24 kHz ==")
    text = await transcribe_at(wy, 24000)
    print(f"  {text!r}")
    assert "quick brown fox" in text.lower(), text
    print("\nALL OK")

asyncio.run(main())
EOF

# API — the models behind one HTTP server

`cmd/serve` is the long-lived process: an OpenAI-shaped API over the models in
this repository, with one flag per vertical deciding what is resident.

    go run ./cmd/serve -llm -embed -tts -stt

`GOALS.md`'s last line — "we will ultimately serve up a HTTP API serving these
features, in Go" — is what this is, and all five verticals are now behind it.

## What answers today

| Endpoint | State |
|---|---|

content.text:
Done. There's a new `wyoming/` package and a `-wyoming` flag on `cmd/serve`.

## What was built

**`wyoming/`** — the protocol, with no dependencies outside the repo:

- `event.go` — the framing: a newline-terminated JSON header, an optional JSON data block, an optional binary payload, with lengths in the header. All three declared lengths are bounded, since a peer's number is a peer's number.
- `info.go` — the event types and the `info` structures, with the exact JSON shapes the reference decoder requires (a missing `attribution` or a `null` where a list belongs is a crash on the client).
- `voices.go` — what a kokoro pack name says about it. `af_heart` → `en-US`, female, labelled "Heart (American English, female)".
- `server.go` — the conversation, plus the accept loop and a drain that unblocks idle reads without cutting an in-flight utterance.

**Wiring** — `cmd/serve -wyoming 0.0.0.0:10300` opens a second listener on the *same* backends: one staging, one GPU queue. `backend.STT` gained a `SampleRate()` accessor, which is the only change to existing model code.

## Decisions worth flagging

- **A flag that takes an address, not a boolean.** Wyoming has nowhere to put a credential, so `-token` cannot reach this port. Which interface it binds is the only control there is, and the startup line says so explicitly.
- **28 voices, not 54.** Misaki's English G2P is the ported one and this protocol has no phoneme field, so a Japanese pack would be a Japanese voice reading English phonemes. `-wyoming-all-voices` offers the rest.
- **Neither streaming direction**, because the numbers say so: 162 ms for a nineteen-second utterance is faster than a satellite could play the first sentence of a streamed one, and kokoro decides all durations at once.
- **Conversion at the door.** Any rate, 8/16/32-bit, any channel count → parakeet's 16 kHz mono through `audio.Resample`. A stream that changes format mid-way is refused rather than concatenated.

## Verified

`go test ./wyoming/` (24 tests, also under `-race`), and then the real thing: the models loaded, driven by upstream's own Python `wyoming==1.10.2` client with both conversations written the way `homeassistant/components/wyoming` writes them.

```
describe    1 asr, 1 tts, 28 voices, 25 asr languages
synthesize  44 chars -> 77 chunks, 3.25 s at 24000 Hz, 35 ms
transcribe  testdata/jfk.wav, 11.00 s -> 108 chars, 46 ms, 236.9x
the loop    speech -> resampled 24k->16k -> transcribed exactly
refusal     unknown voice -> error event, connection survives
```

Cross-checked against the HTTP door: same text and voice, 78000 frames each, **byte for byte the same waveform**. SIGTERM drains with an idle connection held open and releases both ports.

`API.md` and `SPEECH.md` (as W1) document it; `ai.service`'s commented speech line now carries `-wyoming 0.0.0.0:10300`, so the deployment is one uncomment away.

One thing I noticed but did not touch: `API.md`'s flag table still says `-tts-gpu false`, which went stale when T9 flipped the default to true.
